name: Brill's Charged Taub-NUT Spacetime
description: Taub-NUT with an electric charge, the solution of the Einstein-Maxwell equations Dieter Brill found in 1964 as a closed universe filled with gravitational and electromagnetic radiation. It is the Taub-NUT metric at $r_q = 0$ and Reissner and Nordström's at $l = 0$, it has no curvature singularity while $l \neq 0$, and for $r_q^2 > m^2 + l^2$ it has no horizon either and is a wormhole.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ and $G$ explicit; the mass enters as the length $m = GM/c^2$, and the NUT parameter $l$ and the charge radius $r_q$ are lengths.
history: Dieter Brill built a universe with nothing in it but radiation [brill1964]. His solution of the Einstein-Maxwell equations, received from Yale's Sloane Physics Laboratory on 24 September 1963, is "a closed universe of topology $S^3 \times R$, filled with gravitational and electromagnetic radiation" [brill1964]. Space in it is the three dimensional surface of a ball in four dimensions, and wrapped around it is one wave of electric and magnetic field, the lowest mode of such a space [brill1964]. A field that points somewhere cannot look the same in every direction, so the universe is the same at every place and different along different directions, "homogeneous but not isotropic" [brill1964].¶The empty version was twelve years old: Abraham Taub had found in 1951 a closed universe with no matter in it that expands and recollapses [taub1951]. Ezra Newman, Louis Tamburino, and Theodore Unti had found in 1963 the field around a mass with one parameter more than Schwarzschild's, a twist $l$, and Charles Misner had shown that Taub's universe lies behind its horizon, the two being one spacetime [nut1963, misner1963]. Brill's universe is "a generalization of one of the solutions discussed by Taub" [brill1964]. Mass $m$, twist $l$, and charge radius $r_q$ enter through one function, $\Delta = r^2 - 2mr - l^2 + r_q^2$, and at $r_q = 0$ it is Taub-NUT again [clement2016].¶What does the charge do to the black hole? Hans Reissner and Gunnar Nordström's charged hole keeps its charge on a point at $r = 0$ where the curvature is infinite [reissner1916, nordstrom1918, halla2023]. With a twist the point is gone: the sphere at $r = 0$ has the area $4\pi l^2$, the curvature stays finite there, and $r$ runs on to negative values [clement2016]. Gérard Clément, Dmitri Gal'tsov, and Mourad Guenouche called Brill's solution "a regularization of the Reissner-Nordström solution" [clement2016]. While $r_q^2 < m^2 + l^2$ it has two horizons, and Brill's universe is the region between them, where $r$ is the time [clement2016].¶Past $r_q^2 = m^2 + l^2$ the horizons are gone as well [clement2016]. Then $r$ runs from $-\infty$ to $\infty$ through the neck at $r = 0$, and the spacetime is a wormhole that light and observers can cross [clement2016]. Clément, Gal'tsov, and Guenouche pointed it out in 2016, in a case that "surprisingly was not discussed in the literature so far" [clement2016]. Michael Morris and Kip Thorne's wormhole needs matter of negative energy to hold its throat open [morris1988, halla2023]. This one is held open by an electric or magnetic field and nothing else, and Mourad Halla and Volker Perlick call such wormholes "the only known traversable wormhole solutions to Einstein's field equation (in 4 spacetime dimensions) with an energy-momentum tensor that satisfies all energy conditions" [halla2023]. With no point at the centre the electric flux has no source, which is John Wheeler's "charge without charge" [clement2016].¶The twist leaves a line along the axis where the metric is singular, the Misner string, and Misner removed it by making time periodic, which sends a closed timelike curve through every point [misner1963, halla2023]. Clément, Gal'tsov, and Guenouche keep time open and the string with it: geodesics cross the string, and the wormhole is geodesically complete [clement2016]. Closed timelike curves remain near the string [clement2016]. Clément and Guenouche found two years later, for a class of these spacetimes, that a charged particle coming in from far away never closes its path [clement2018]. Could a ship go through? A body two metres across feels a tidal pull of one Earth gravity at the throat for $l$ of half a light second, $1.5 \times 10^8$ m, but an electric field weak enough to leave the ship's atoms whole needs $l$ of a tenth of a light year [clement2016].

related.text: Brill's spacetime with the charge taken away, $r_q = 0$. His universe is then Taub's and his black hole is NUT space [brill1964, clement2016].

Brill's spacetime with the twist taken out, $l = 0$ and $r_s = 2m$. The curvature at $r = 0$ is then infinite, and too much charge leaves a naked singularity where Brill's metric has a wormhole [clement2016].
The wormhole held open by matter of negative energy. Brill's, at $r_q^2 > m^2 + l^2$, is held open by an electromagnetic field, with a Misner string along its axis [morris1988, clement2016].
At $r_q^2 = m^2 + l^2$ the two horizons meet at $r = m$, and Brill's black hole is the single source of complex mass among Israel, Wilson, and Perjés's fields [clement2016, hartle1972].
Taub-NUT set spinning, where Brill's is Taub-NUT with a charge. Jerzy Plebański and Marek Demiański's family of 1976 holds both [plebanski1976, griffiths2005].
Dieter Brill's other space with nothing in it but field: one moment of a universe of gravitational waves alone, from 1959, whose mass he proved positive [brill1959].

coordinates.name: Spherical
domains: r \in \left(m + \sqrt{m^2 + l^2 - r_q^2},\, \infty\right) \;\text{for}\; r_q^2 \le m^2 + l^2
\Delta = 0 \;\text{(the horizons } r_\pm = m \pm \sqrt{m^2 + l^2 - r_q^2}\text{, present for } r_q^2 \le m^2 + l^2\text{)}

parameters.description: Geometric mass, $m = GM/c^2$, a length
NUT parameter, a length, the gravitomagnetic monopole moment; at $l = 0$ the metric is Reissner and Nordström's

Charge radius, a length, with $r_q^2 = Q^2G/(4\pi\epsilon_0c^4)$ for a charge $Q$; an electric and a magnetic charge enter through the sum of their squares, and at $r_q = 0$ the metric is the Taub-NUT metric
The area of the sphere of constant $t$ and $r$ divided by $4\pi$, which is never less than $l^2$
Its roots are the horizons $r_\pm = m \pm \sqrt{m^2 + l^2 - r_q^2}$, which exist for $r_q^2 \le m^2 + l^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and a Misner string on each half of the axis, and write $\Sigma$ and $\Delta$ as the parameters define them. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.kretschmann: K = \dfrac{8r_q^4}{\Sigma^4} + \dfrac{48\left(\left(m^2 - l^2\right)\left(r^6 - 15l^2r^4 + 15l^4r^2 - l^6\right) - 2mr\left(\left(r_q^2 - 6l^2\right)r^4 - 10l^2\left(r_q^2 - 2l^2\right)r^2 + l^4\left(5r_q^2 - 6l^2\right)\right) + r_q^2\left(\left(r_q^2 - 10l^2\right)r^4 - 2l^2\left(3r_q^2 - 10l^2\right)r^2 + l^4\left(r_q^2 - 2l^2\right)\right)\right)}{\Sigma^6}

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t_N, r, \theta, \phi)$ with $t_N = t + 2l\phi/c$, the time in which the northern half of the axis is regular and one Misner string lies along $\theta = \pi$, and write $\Sigma$ and $\Delta$ as the parameters define them. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct_N$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t_N}$ means $d(ct_N)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.kretschmann: K = \dfrac{8r_q^4}{\Sigma^4} + \dfrac{48\left(\left(m^2 - l^2\right)\left(r^6 - 15l^2r^4 + 15l^4r^2 - l^6\right) - 2mr\left(\left(r_q^2 - 6l^2\right)r^4 - 10l^2\left(r_q^2 - 2l^2\right)r^2 + l^4\left(5r_q^2 - 6l^2\right)\right) + r_q^2\left(\left(r_q^2 - 10l^2\right)r^4 - 2l^2\left(3r_q^2 - 10l^2\right)r^2 + l^4\left(r_q^2 - 2l^2\right)\right)\right)}{\Sigma^6}
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{\Delta\left(r\,\Sigma - m\,\Sigma - r\,\Delta\right)}{\Sigma^3}\dot{t_N}^2 + \dfrac{4l\,\Delta\left(\cos\theta - 1\right)\left(r\,\Sigma - m\,\Sigma - r\,\Delta\right)}{\Sigma^3}\dot{t_N}\dot{\phi} - \dfrac{r\,\Sigma - m\,\Sigma - r\,\Delta}{\Sigma\,\Delta}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r\,\Delta}{\Sigma}\dot{\theta}^2 + \dfrac{\Delta\left(\cos\theta - 1\right)\left(r\,\Sigma^2\cos\theta + r\,\Sigma^2 + 4l^2\,r\,\Sigma\cos\theta - 4l^2\,r\,\Sigma - 4m\,l^2\,\Sigma\cos\theta + 4m\,l^2\,\Sigma - 4l^2\,r\,\Delta\cos\theta + 4l^2\,r\,\Delta\right)}{\Sigma^3}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Brill's Universe

parameters.description: Geometric mass, $m = GM/c^2$, a length
NUT parameter, a length, the gravitomagnetic monopole moment; at $l = 0$ the metric is Reissner and Nordström's

Charge radius, a length, with $r_q^2 = Q^2G/(4\pi\epsilon_0c^4)$ for a charge $Q$; an electric and a magnetic charge enter through the sum of their squares, and at $r_q = 0$ the metric is the Taub-NUT metric
The area of the sphere of constant $\tau$ and $\psi$ divided by $4\pi$
Positive between its roots $\tau_\pm = m \pm \sqrt{m^2 + l^2 - r_q^2}$, where the universe begins and ends

coordinates.convention: We use the time $\tau$, a length, and the Euler angles $(\psi, \theta, \phi)$ of the sphere $S^3$, for $r_q^2 < m^2 + l^2$, and write $\Sigma$ and $U$ as the parameters define them. The region is the one between the horizons, with $\tau = r$ and $2l\psi = ct$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = \tau$.
coordinates.kretschmann: K = \dfrac{8r_q^4}{\Sigma^4} + \dfrac{48\left(\left(m^2 - l^2\right)\left(\tau^6 - 15l^2\tau^4 + 15l^4\tau^2 - l^6\right) - 2m\tau\left(\left(r_q^2 - 6l^2\right)\tau^4 - 10l^2\left(r_q^2 - 2l^2\right)\tau^2 + l^4\left(5r_q^2 - 6l^2\right)\right) + r_q^2\left(\left(r_q^2 - 10l^2\right)\tau^4 - 2l^2\left(3r_q^2 - 10l^2\right)\tau^2 + l^4\left(r_q^2 - 2l^2\right)\right)\right)}{\Sigma^6}
